messages:
Anna: FYI - noticed a small but consistent quality delta when enabling the new FP8 kernel on L40S for the 13B long-context canary. Affects AWQ quantized weights more than GPTQ. Numbers: ~0.8-1.1% drop on long-prefix exact-match, smaller on short prompts. :eyes:
Mike: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro and the configs you used?
Anna: yeah. quick summary:
- model: redwood/13b-beta (onboarding branch)
- hw: L40S, driver 535.xx
- kernel: fp8-tilerefactor-v2 enabled + mixed-precision path on
- quant: AWQ 4bit + activation scaling tweaks
- eval: longseq synthetic suite (2k prefixes, avg 1024 context)
- delta: EM down 0.8-1.1%, perplexity +3-6

Repro command:
```bash
./run_canary.sh --model redwood/13b-beta \
  --quant awq --bits 4 \
  --runtime kernel=fp8-tilerefactor-v2,mp=true \
  --device l40s --eval longseq_suite \
```
Logs snippet (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-19T22:05:12Z] kv-cache: reuse hit 91%
[2026-03-19T22:05:14Z] kernel: fp8 tiling applied, tile_size=128
[2026-03-19T22:05:18Z] decode: bad_token_penalty spike at token 512 (seq-specific)
```
Mike: interesting the spike at token 512. sounds like a runlength/prefix boundary issue where FP8 scale estimates drift mid-sequence. Did you run with kv-prefix-caching off/on?
Anna: tried both. with kv-prefix-caching on, latency improved but quality delta persisted. with caching off the delta shrank by ~0.2% but still present.
Sanjay: could be activation saturation in the attention projection after many steps. FP8 dynamic range is tight; AWQ's per-group scales might not adjust for long accumulation. Have you inspected activation histograms?
Anna: attaching a quick tracelet dump (trimmed) showing activation mean/std over the heads at steps 480-520. The mean drifts ~12% on head 7.
Eva: thanks. can you also run the same canary on H100 with identical config? if it's purely fp8-range-related we might see different behavior due to kernel numerical tiling and cuBLAS differences.
Anna: on it. queued a run for H100; ETA ~20m.

(20 minutes later)
Anna: H100 run done. no measurable EM drop on H100 for the same AWQ+fp8 config. delta basically 0.0-0.1% on longseq. So hardware/runtime interaction likely.
Mike: good signal. suggests L40S kernel path has a tiling/accumulation quirk for long KV sequences. evicting kv-chunks or changing tile_size might matter. can we try tile_size=256 or enable runqueue-split?
Sanjay: also try forcing per-channel rescale at runtime for attention matmul outputs as a short-term mitigation. i.e. rescale_before_softmax=true with clamp=127 for fp8. won't be perfect but worth testing.
Anna: quick experiments:
- tile_size=256: delta reduced to ~0.3%
- runqueue-split=true: delta ~0.25% but +8% p99 latency
- rescale_before_softmax=true,clamp=127: delta ~0.15% and latency +2%

Eva: tradeoffs seem reasonable for canary. For rollout we should: 1) keep H100 default fp8 enablement, 2) mark L40S fp8 as opt-in with tile_size=256 and rescale mitigation, 3) create a runtime auto-detect that switches to the safer path when long prefixes seen.
Mike: agreed. please open an action ticket with exact config flags and perf/quality numbers. also add a small eval that exercises steps 400-800 so we catch future regressions in CI.
Anna: created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8241 (details + traces attached).
Sanjay: one more note — AWQ's scale clipping at quant-time might interact badly with activation outliers. let's run a small experiment: AWQ re-run with per-group clipping disabled, keep runtime rescale. could reveal whether quantization or runtime accumulation is dominant.
Anna: queued. also adding a micro-eval measuring headwise mean drift over long prefixes.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment "fp8-tilerefactor-v2" started on cluster-l40s-canary (3 nodes). Monitor: /ops/canaries/fp8-tilerefactor-v2.
Mike: thanks. keep this thread updated. if L40S shows regression outside 0.2% threshold in next 24h we rollback to fp8-tilerefactor-v1 for L40S.
Anna: ack. will post final numbers and go/no-go update tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:
